newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures called steady to slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures called steady to slightly lower.

text.p: IPE oil futures were expected to start the week's trade unchanged to slightly lower after Friday's sharp fall when hurricane damage fears in the Gulf of Mexico eased, brokers said on Monday.
IPE Brent was called steady to five cents lower from the September contract's $18.12 a barrel settle last week, with the momentum of Friday's 57 cent fall continuing a little.

IPE gas oil was anticipated opening flat to 50 cents or a $1 lower. It closed on Friday at $163.50 a tonne, down $3.50 on the day, and may slide further to catch up with the damage done to Brent and WTI numbers after it stopped trading last week.
IPE futures lifted and then fell sharply last week as Hurricane Danny loomed off the U.S. Gulf Coast, threatened to badly damage oil installations, and then passed by peacefully.
"There was also some long liquidation ahead of the U.N. meeting," said one broker.

Few players wanted to begin Monday's trade exposed, with the U.N. expected to receive the Iraqi aid distribution plan. Its approval will clear the way for Baghdad to export crude again under its "oil-for-food" deal with the U.N.
"We see it as stable with a downward bias after the U.N. meeting, after which it should find some buying again," said one broker.
But it was unclear if the U.N. would meet immediately to approve the plan on Monday or if some time would be needed to digest and discuss its details.

Brokers said they would also be watching the North Sea carefully, where problems at the Nelson field have already pushed some 1.25 million barrels from the Forties loading programme for July into August.
Worsening North Sea problems or memories of last week's bullish draw on U.S. gasoline stocks could help keep IPE Brent above $17.84, the next critical support level, brokers said.
